references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, Moses says that the Lord will give meat in the evening and bread in the morning, which directly corresponds with the promise in verse 12.
The fulfillment of the promise of meat in the evening, when quails came and covered the camp.
Moses and Aaron tell the people that they shall know that the Lord brought them out of Egypt, and that they shall see the glory of the Lord.
Another account of how the Lord sent quails to the people of Israel in the wilderness.
The psalmist describes how God let manna rain down from heaven and gave them bread from heaven.
The psalmist tells how God let meat rain down like dust, and birds like the sand of the sea.
The psalmist reminds that God sent quails and satisfied the people with bread from heaven.
God's promise that Israel shall know that He is the Lord their God, who brought them out of Egypt.
The Lord declares that the people shall know that He is the Lord their God.
Jesus refers to the bread from heaven that the fathers ate in the wilderness, and explains that the true bread comes from the Father.
Paul refers to how all ate the same spiritual food, making reference to the manna in the wilderness.
The same historical event (the gift of meat) described from two angles: the promise and its fulfillment.
